mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in industrial production (INDPRO) and a fall in the housing starts index (HOUST) over two months indicates a shift from cyclical goods to housing stagnation, which historically precedes a mild equity pullback over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 0% change and HOUST < 0% change for two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO rises and HOUST falls simultaneously for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 1% during a recession signals an aggressive easing cycle, which boosts risk appetite and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: deep recession with aggressive central bank easing
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS falls below 1% and UNRATE exceeds 6%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in real personal income (PAYEMS) and consumer spending (proxied by RSAFS) above their respective 12-month averages signals robust demand growth, which supports earnings and justifies positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and RSAFS exceed their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decrease in the unemployment rate below 4% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and inflation risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as discount rates rise.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE remains below 4% for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month average, combined with a stable inflation rate (CPIAUCSL change < 0.2% monthly), signals improving supply without inflationary pressure, which supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to improved earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-mo avg and CPIAUCSL monthly change < 0.2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when INDPRO exceeds its 12-month average and CPIAUCSL changes by less than 0.2% monthly.
